notes: Meta serves the ENTIRE job catalogue in ONE GraphQL POST (CareersJobSearchResultsV2DataQuery): all_jobs had 801 entries, exactly matching the site's own job_count=801 (CareersJobSearchHideFiltersBarV2Query). No pagination.

The POST is fully forgeable from plain httpx with NO cookies and NO real tokens: the lsd body param + x-fb-lsd header are required to be PRESENT but their value is not validated for logged-out traffic — this recipe ships a made-up constant ('AdSrecipereplay000') that returned HTTP 200 + 801 jobs. What IS validated is a plausible Chrome header set: without sec-ch-ua/Sec-Fetch-* headers Meta answers HTTP 400 for every route, including plain GETs.

replay.py's http_json runner sends POST bodies as JSON, which Meta rejects (HTTP 400, proven), but Meta's www stack reads request params from the query string on POST — so ALL form params live in entrypoint.url and the JSON body '{}' replay sends is ignored. Proven via replay._request directly (captures/meta/forge_test5.py, variant M).

doc_id=27129360303422352 is the persisted-query id: it survives lsd/session churn but WILL eventually rotate with Meta frontend releases. When it dies this recipe fails LOUDLY (HTTP 400/GraphQL error -> RecipeExecutionError), never silently. Re-discovery: load /jobs in a browser, grab the new doc_id from the CareersJobSearchResultsV2DataQuery POST.

expected_min_jobs=500 vs 801 today: a partial-capture regression (server-side pagination appearing) would return a page-sized fraction (25/50/100), far below 500, while 500 still tolerates ~35% genuine catalogue shrink.
fields.url uses the stable public /jobs/{id} form, which 301s to the current canonical route (today /profile/job_details/{id}/); pinning the redirect target would be less durable.
Job records carry no posted/updated timestamp in this payload — first_seen tracking must come from our side.
